subject.title: vllm openai-completions streaming parser drops tool_calls when reasoning_content streams first for gpt-oss-120b at large systemPrompt

question: Should OpenClaw require an exact current-main vLLM gpt-oss stream fixture before accepting any recovery path that could reclassify assistant text as executable tool calls?
rationale: The reduced source path appears covered, while the proposed fallback recovery affects tool-execution safety and depends on whether maintainers consider the reporter's historical stream evidence sufficient.

options.title: Require Exact Stream Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a redacted current-main SSE fixture or live vLLM gpt-oss reproduction proves the failure, then fix only that parser path.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Recovery
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned vLLM/gpt-oss-specific recovery design before exact reproduction, with explicit false-positive tests and security review.

options.title: Defer To Existing Workarounds
options.body: Treat the vLLM `tool_choice` guidance and adjacent parser fixes as enough only if maintainers decide this deployment class is not a core blocker without new proof.

recommendation.title: Require Exact Stream Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a redacted current-main SSE fixture or live vLLM gpt-oss reproduction proves the failure, then fix only that parser path.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and adjacent parser history make Vincent Koc the best available owner for the proof-sufficiency and parser-boundary decision.
